title: LG Uplus, GS Neotek to Integrate Enterprise Security Platforms - www.thelec.net
content: LG Uplus is pursuing the integration of GS Neotek’s cloud security service, Security Lens, into its enterprise network security platform, U+SASE. The goal is to enable corporate security administrators to monitor the security status of cloud servers, as well as employees’ work devices and access networks, through a single platform. LG Uplus and GS Neotek signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) on security business cooperation at LG Uplus’s headquarters in Yongsan, Seoul, on Nov. 9. U+SASE protects employee devices and networks when users access corporate systems or the web. Security Lens checks servers and data within cloud environments for security vulnerabilities and analyzes system logs. It also monitors systems operated in companies’ own data centers. The two companies plan to expand their cooperation to include AlphaKey, an integrated identity management service; U+ Safe AI, which prevents data leakage during AI use; and security threat detection and response services. They also agreed to develop plans for reselling security products and conducting joint sales activities.

title: Is Goldman Sachs an Attractive Investment Option Heading into 2027? - The Globe and Mail
content: The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. GS appears well-positioned heading into 2027, supported by strong investment banking (IB) performance, resilient trading revenues and continued growth in its asset and wealth management business. Improving capital markets activity, healthy dealmaking momentum and increasing demand for alternative investments are expected to support revenue growth and profitability. The company's focus on operating efficiency and disciplined capital management strengthens its long-term growth prospects. However, a potential moderation in merger and acquisition (M&A) activity in 2027, coupled with policy and regulatory uncertainties following the 2026 U.S. midterm elections, could dampen investment banking momentum. Elevated expenses and macroeconomic headwinds pose additional challenges. Given these mixed factors, investors may be wondering whether Goldman is still an attractive investment opportunity heading into 2027 or not. To answer this, let us delve deeper. Goldman continues to benefit from the recovery in global IB activity, supported by increased M&A, initial public offerings, and underwriting volumes. The momentum was also evident in the first nine months of 2026, with IB fees jumping 40% year over year to $9.46 billion. Advisory revenues rose 34% to $4.53 billion, while equity and debt underwriting revenues increased 73% and 29% to $2.19 billion and $2.75 billion, respectively. Looking ahead, Goldman's leadership position and robust deal pipeline bode well for continued growth. The company has maintained its #1 position in announced and completed M&A volumes and equity underwriting year to date, advising on $1.5 trillion in announced M&A transactions. Despite strong revenue generation in the third quarter, management indicated that its investment banking backlog remains robust, supported by sustained client engagement and replenishment in equity underwriting. Management continues to view the capital markets environment favorably, with opportunities arising from strategic dealmaking, technology investments and AI infrastructure financing. Although slower M&A activity in 2027 could constrain advisory fee growth, GS's strong dealmaking franchise and sponsor relationships position it to benefit, potentially cushioning the impacts of weaker overall transaction volumes. Similar to Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan JPM and Morgan Stanley MS could face pressure on investment banking (IB) fee growth amid a potential M&A slowdown in 2027. While softer dealmaking activity may constrain advisory revenues for both banks, rising private equity exits and alternative liquidity transactions could provide some offset. The growing adoption of continuation funds and secondary transactions could create advisory opportunities, particularly for Morgan Stanley. Goldman continues to streamline its operations by exiting non-core consumer banking businesses and strengthening its core franchises. Under CEO David Solomon, the company has been strategically shifting its focus toward Global Banking & Markets (GBM) and Asset & Wealth Management (AWM), wherein it maintains strong competitive advantages and sees opportunities to build more durable revenue streams. In sync with these efforts, in August 2026, Goldman announced an agreement to acquire NEOS Investments, a provider of derivative income exchange-traded funds (ETFs). The acquisition is expected to increase Goldman's global active ETF assets under supervision to more than $90 billion, positioning it among the top eight providers by assets. The company also announced an agreement to acquire LCN Capital Partners, expanding its private real estate investment capabilities. In April 2026, Goldman acquired Innovator Capital Management, strengthening its active ETF offerings. In the same month, it completed the divestiture of its Polish asset management business, Goldman Sachs TFI, to ING Bank Slaski. These initiatives complement its broader efforts to reduce exposure to non-core consumer banking operations, including the transition of the General Motors credit card program in 2025 and the planned transfer of the Apple Card program to JPMorgan. The benefits of Goldman's strategic repositioning are increasingly evident in its financial performance. For the first nine months of 2026, GBM revenues jumped 34% year over year to $41.72 billion, while AWM revenues rose 15% to $13.73 billion. Management highlighted that durable revenues have more than doubled since its 2020 Investor Day and accounted for approximately 45% of the total revenues in the first nine months of 2026. These developments reflect Goldman's progress in building a more diversified earnings base, improving revenue stability and strengthening its long-term growth prospects. Goldman continues to accelerate its firmwide artificial intelligence transformation, focusing on improving productivity, streamlining operations and driving long-term operating leverage. The company is integrating AI across its core businesses, including trading, investment banking, asset management and internal operations, to enhance efficiency and strengthen its competitive position. In July 2026, Goldman's Asset Management unit launched AlphaAI, an AI-focused investment platform designed to capitalize on AI-driven investment opportunities across public and private markets. In May 2026, Goldman partnered with Anthropic, Blackstone and Hellman & Friedman to establish a $1.5-billion AI services venture designed to accelerate AI adoption across portfolio companies. These initiatives underscore the company's efforts to leverage AI for both investment opportunities and operational improvements. At the center of Goldman's transformation are One Goldman Sachs 3.0 (OneGS 3.0) and the GS AI Assistant program. OneGS 3.0 is a multi-year initiative focused on embedding AI into the company's operating model by simplifying workflows, automating processes, modernizing infrastructure and improving data management. Meanwhile, the GS AI Assistant is designed to enhance employee productivity by supporting information analysis, content generation and routine tasks, allowing professionals to focus on higher-value activities and client engagement. During the third-quarter 2026 earnings call, management highlighted significant opportunities arising from growing AI infrastructure investments, particularly increased demand for data centers and computing capacity. Goldman expects its financing, advisory and investment capabilities to position it favorably to capitalize on these opportunities. However, management also emphasized the need for disciplined underwriting and prudent risk management as AI-related financing requirements expand. Goldman's focus on operating efficiency is also reflected in its latest results. In the first nine months of 2026, the company's efficiency ratio improved to 59.4% from 62.1% in the year-ago period, reflecting better operating leverage and aligning with its 60% target. While investments in AI and technology may keep expenses elevated in the near term, continued automation and process improvements could enhance scalability, support revenue growth and strengthen long-term profitability. Goldman maintains a strong balance sheet, supported by robust liquidity and capital levels. Its solid financial position allows the company to return capital to shareholders through share repurchases and regular dividend payments while maintaining sufficient flexibility to support business expansion. As of Sept. 30, 2026, Goldman's deposits totaled $568 billion, up from $558 billion as of June 30, 2026. Unsecured long-term borrowings stood at $352 billion. The company's average global core liquid assets increased to $574 billion in the third quarter from $555 billion in the preceding quarter, providing a substantial liquidity cushion. Meanwhile, its standardized Common Equity Tier 1 capital ratio stood at 12.4%, 100 basis points above the current regulatory requirement of 11.4%. Following the Federal Reserve's 2026 stress test, GS increased its quarterly common stock dividend by 11% to $5 per share. Similarly, JPMorgan announced a 10% increase in its quarterly dividend to $1.65 per share in September. Morgan Stanley increased its quarterly dividend by 15% to $1.15 per share in the third quarter of 2026. Coming back to GS, in the first quarter of 2025, the board had approved a share repurchase program of up to $40 billion of common stock. As of Sept. 30, 2026, Goldman had nearly $19 billion worth of shares available under authorization. Supported by robust liquidity, solid earnings generation and capital levels above regulatory requirements, Goldman appears well-positioned to sustain shareholder-friendly capital distributions while pursuing growth opportunities. However, the pace of future buybacks will depend on regulatory capital requirements and business investment needs. Over the past seven days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 and 2027 earnings has remained unchanged. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Goldman's 2026 and 2027 earnings implies year-over-year growth of 39.3% and 3.4%, respectively. The GS stock currently trades at a discount to the industry. The stock is trading at a forward price/earnings (P/E) of 12.32X, below the industry average of 12.34X. Its peers JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley are trading at a P/E of 13.26X and 14.36X, respectively. Shares of Goldman have gained 3.1% year to date, outperforming the industry's 0.6% rise but lagging JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley, which have rallied 6.2% and 5.4%, respectively. Goldman's strong investment banking pipeline, resilient trading performance and growing Asset & Wealth Management revenues support its earnings prospects. AI-driven efficiency initiatives and a solid capital position further strengthen its growth potential and shareholder returns. However, elevated expenses, weakness in fixed-income trading and macroeconomic uncertainties remain concerns. Further an expected slowdown in earnings growth from 39.3% in 2026 to 3.4% in 2027, may limit near-term upside. Given these factors, existing investors should retain GS shares, while new investors may wait for a more attractive entry point. Currently, GS carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). title: Suzuki increases GS 150 and GD 110s prices by Rs10,000 in Pakistan - Pkrevenue.com
content: Pak Suzuki has revised the prices of its two popular motorcycles without issuing a public announcement, making both models more expensive by Rs10,000. Pak Suzuki Motor Company has increased the prices of two popular motorcycles in Pakistan, the Suzuki GS 150 and Suzuki GD 110s.Pakistan economic news The latest price revision adds Rs10,000 to the cost of each model, increasing the purchasing expense for customers planning to buy either motorcycle. The company has made the changes without issuing an official public announcement or sharing a detailed explanation for the decision. Instead, the revised prices were quietly updated on Pak Suzuki’s official website, where customers can now find the latest rates. Following the adjustment, the Suzuki GS 150 is now available at Rs409,900, compared to its previous price of Rs399,900. Similarly, the Suzuki GD 110s has become more expensive, with its price increasing from Rs369,900 to Rs379,900. Both motorcycles have received an identical price increase of Rs10,000. Although the adjustment is relatively similar in monetary terms, it adds to the overall cost for buyers considering these popular commuter and everyday riding options. The Suzuki GS 150 is known for its larger engine capacity and suitability for riders looking for a motorcycle for both routine commuting and longer journeys. Meanwhile, the GD 110s is positioned as a smaller-capacity option for everyday urban transportation. The latest revision means customers will now have to arrange additional funds to purchase either motorcycle. However, Pak Suzuki has not clarified whether the increase is linked to higher production expenses, currency fluctuations, manufacturing costs, or other business considerations. The absence of a formal announcement also leaves customers without an official explanation for the revised prices. With this adjustment, prospective buyers should check the latest prices with authorised Suzuki dealerships before finalising their purchases, as the updated figures are now reflected on the company’s website.

NINGBO, ZHEJIANG, CHINA, November 10, 2026 /EINPresswire.com/ — When European procurement managers evaluate cleaning appliances for retail shelves, expectations have shifted away from superficial aesthetic appeal toward rigorous safety verification. In home cleaning and textile maintenance sectors, electrical safety, temperature rise control, and mechanical protection have become strict baseline metrics. Buyers no longer select products based solely on suction power numbers; instead, they examine how internal components withstand continuous operational stress. Within this shifting trade environment, Yiwu Saiwei Household Appliances Co., Ltd. (Amare) has established a robust operational foothold by aligning manufacturing precision with international safety expectations. As a specialized enterprise focusing on textile maintenance devices, Amare operates as a China leading carpet spot cleaning machine supplier, addressing the rigorous demands of global distribution networks through systematic quality control. The contemporary supply chain environment places considerable emphasis on verifiable reliability at the factory level. Retailers across Western Europe and North America scrutinize supplier credentials down to individual component tolerances and circuit board layouts. When sourcing a carpet spot cleaning machine, procurement teams look for manufacturers who can demonstrate consistent output without compromising on electrical insulation or thermal management. This operational reality requires production facilities to maintain tight tolerances during plastic injection molding, motor assembly, and wiring harness installation. By integrating advanced testing instruments directly into production lines, manufacturing plants can filter out potential defects before final packaging. The Significance of GS Certification in European Markets Quality assurance frameworks in export destinations rely heavily on recognized third-party safety marks. The GS mark, standing for Geprüfte Sicherheit, represents an authoritative German safety certification recognized throughout the European Union. Tested strictly against European Norm standards by accredited independent testing institutions, this mark verifies that a product meets statutory safety requirements regarding mechanical strength, electrical insulation, ergonomic design, and chemical composition. Although the GS mark is technically voluntary under European product legislation, major German retailers, DIY warehouse chains, and regional distributors treat it as a mandatory prerequisite for market entry. Compared to the CE marking, which relies primarily on manufacturer self-declaration, the GS mark requires factory inspections and independent laboratory testing of physical samples. This distinction makes GS certification a formidable benchmark for overseas suppliers seeking entry into premium retail channels. Retail buyers recognize that products bearing this safety mark have undergone rigorous evaluation regarding potential hazards such as short circuits, overheating, user burns, and toxic material emissions. Consequently, achieving GS compliance transforms a standard household appliance into a trusted consumer commodity. Manufacturers who invest in this certification demonstrate a long-term commitment to consumer protection and regulatory transparency, distinguishing their offerings in crowded retail environments. How Precision Manufacturing Supports GS Compliance Meeting stringent German safety standards requires meticulous attention to engineering and internal component design. At its manufacturing facility in Zhejiang, Yiwu Saiwei Household Appliances Co., Ltd. implements dedicated engineering protocols to ensure that every device meets mechanical and electrical safety requirements. The company’s core product lineup includes versatile 500W spot cleaning units engineered for deep textile extraction. These compact machines utilize proprietary self-developed water pumps and heating elements designed to balance cleaning efficiency with thermal stability during extended operation cycles. To prevent fluid ingress into sensitive electrical compartments, these 500W units feature a deliberate clean and wastewater separation architecture. The dual-tank configuration isolates fresh cleaning solution from extracted wastewater, preventing cross-contamination and reducing the risk of internal short circuits. Furthermore, integrated overflow prevention sensors automatically halt water intake when recovery tanks reach maximum capacity. Motor overheating protection mechanisms monitor operational temperatures in real time, cutting power supply automatically if thermal thresholds are exceeded due to restricted airflow or extended continuous use. Beyond internal fluid dynamics, the structural integrity of the appliance plays a critical role in mechanical safety. Precision metal and plastic molds ensure that housing components maintain exact wall thicknesses and tight assembly clearances. This dimensional consistency eliminates loose panel gaps where moisture or dust could penetrate internal circuitry. Strain reliefs on power cords and secure internal wiring harnesses prevent wire fraying or disconnection under mechanical vibration. By combining robust thermal management, precise fluid isolation, and durable mechanical housing, Amare ensures that its carpet spot cleaning machine achieves the structural reliability necessary to pass rigorous GS laboratory evaluations. A credible safety certification is only as reliable as the manufacturing consistency behind it. To maintain continuous compliance with European standards, export suppliers must implement comprehensive batch tracking and quality traceability systems. In modern factory operations, accountability extends from raw material intake to final packaging and palletization. Each manufactured unit receives a unique laser-etched serial number and production batch barcode, linking the finished appliance to specific material lots, component suppliers, and assembly shift logs. When independent auditors inspect production facilities for GS surveillance audits, they examine these traceability records to verify that mass-produced items match the exact specifications of the original tested prototype. Critical components such as thermostats, power switches, pump motors, and internal wiring cables are sourced from qualified tier-one suppliers with verifiable material test reports. Yiwu Saiwei Household Appliances Co., Ltd. archives all incoming material inspection certificates and end-of-line electrical safety test logs in a centralized digital database. This rigorous documentation process enables channel distributors and retail buyers to trace safety data instantly if quality inquiries arise. If a specific batch requires verification, quality assurance personnel can retrieve electrical insulation test results, high-voltage breakdown test records, and functional test logs within minutes. This level of operational transparency reassures commercial partners that product safety is managed through systematic engineering protocols rather than random spot checks. Such structured traceability reinforces long-term trust between Chinese manufacturing enterprises and international trade partners. title: Suzuki GS 150 and GD 110s Prices Increased by Rs10,000 - Pakwheels
content: Suzuki has increased the prices of two of its popular motorcycles, the Suzuki GS 150 and GD 110s, by Rs10,000 each.  The company increased the prices without a public announcement. They quietly updated the figures on their website and have not given any reason for the increase. Following the latest revision, the Suzuki GS 150 now costs Rs409,900, up from Rs399,900. Meanwhile, the Suzuki GD 110s is now priced at Rs379,900, up from Rs369,900. Here is a comparison of the previous and revised prices: Both motorcycles have received an identical price increase of Rs10,000. In percentage terms, the GS 150 has become about 2.5% more expensive, while the GD 110s has increased by around 2.7%. The new price also pushes the GS 150 above Rs400,000. That is a lot of money for a motorcycle that has changed very little since 2006, when it was launched in Pakistan. There’s no denying that the GS 150 is a reliable bike. Its plush ride, dependable OHC engine, and strong resale value are among the reasons it remains one of the best-selling 150cc bikes in Pakistan, but it lacks many features that other 150cc bikes offer these days. Even at Rs409,900, buyers don’t get a fuel gauge, gear position indicator, alloy wheels, or a return-shift gear system. Suzuki changes only the stickers on the GS 150 every year, without any upgrades. On the other hand, motorcycles such as the United CCR150 and Royal GPX Libre 150 offer all those features at a lower price point. Suzuki still has the edge in resale value and its reputation for reliability. However, spending more than Rs400,000 on a motorcycle with an older design and fewer features may be hard to justify for the value. The GD 110s is in a different position. It’s a 110cc motorcycle that falls in the 100cc category but offers features that other mainstream bikes in this segment, like the Honda Pridor, don’t. It gets alloy rims, self-start, a balancer shaft, a balancer shaft engine, a gear indicator, and a dipper switch, and no other bike in this segment offers this list of features. That’s also why the Rs10,000 increase may not change much for people already planning to buy a GD 110s. Of course, Rs379,900 is still a high price for a 110cc motorcycle. But unlike the GS 150, which faces several alternatives, the GD 110s has little direct competition in its category. What do you think about Suzuki’s latest price increase? title: GS Engineering & Construction to verify all ready-mix plants for winter concrete quality - Chosunbiz
content: GS Engineering & Construction will launch preemptive quality control from the ready-mix supply stage to secure concrete quality during the winter. GS Engineering & Construction said on the 10th it will run advance performance verification tests on all ready-mix plants set to supply cold-weather concrete to its construction sites this winter. The core change goes beyond the existing practice of checking quality after delivery to the site: the company will directly verify the performance of concrete produced at each ready-mix plant before delivery and allow only plants that meet its quality standards to supply. In winter, if concrete freezes in low temperatures, it can compromise the quality of poured structures. To prevent this, builders have mainly used tents and hot-air heaters. But that approach has limits, causing schedule delays and making steady quality hard to secure. In response, GS Engineering & Construction is expanding the use of "cold-weather concrete," which can achieve reliable strength below freezing without special equipment. The technology uses rapid-hardening cement, which gains strength faster than ordinary cement, together with special admixtures, so the concrete will not freeze and can reach the required strength even with only a plastic cover. Because cold-weather concrete demands stricter quality control than ordinary concrete, advance verification is essential to confirm whether each ready-mix plant can meet the required concrete quality. Accordingly, since Oct. 12, GS Engineering & Construction has begun advance performance verification on all ready-mix plants slated to supply cold-weather concrete to its sites. Key checks include ▲ the basic properties of the concrete ▲ whether freeze damage occurs at subzero temperatures ▲ and concrete strength evaluation. GS Engineering & Construction will directly confirm whether the concrete each plant produces meets set quality standards, and it plans to bar plants that fall short from delivering cold-weather concrete to its sites. This verification is meaningful because GS Engineering & Construction will carry it out using its own research and testing infrastructure. With an in-house lab capable of performance verification and specialized technical staff, the company has a system to test each ready-mix plant's performance directly without relying on external testing agencies. The company plans to strengthen this preemptive quality-control system by identifying potential quality variations at the production stage and supplying only verified materials to its sites. title: Coontec’s AEZIZ v3.0 Wins GS Certification, Targets Public Sector - THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media
content: Coontec said on Nov. 9 that its software and artificial intelligence (AI) supply chain security platform, AEZIZ v3.0, has received Grade 1 Good Software (GS) certification from Korea Testing Certification (KTC). The company plans to strengthen its supply chain security business targeting public institutions and financial companies. The AEZIZ v3.0 feature that met the Grade 1 GS certification requirements is software composition analysis (SCA). SCA identifies and analyzes open-source components, licenses and security vulnerabilities in software. In addition to SCA, AEZIZ offers supply chain management (SCM), open-source intake management (RMS) and AI component analysis (AICA). The platform can analyze binary files as well as source code. Binary files are program files converted from source code into a format that computers can execute. This allows the platform to analyze third-party commercial software even when source code is difficult to obtain. GS certification is a national certification program that evaluates software quality. It assesses functional suitability, performance efficiency, usability, reliability, security and maintainability. Grade 1-certified products qualify for preferential procurement of commercial software by public institutions. Coontec uses data on more than 8.6 million software components and over 400,000 vulnerabilities in its analysis. The platform also generates software bills of materials (SBOMs), which list software components, in international standard formats. It can also generate AI bills of materials (AI-BOMs) showing library dependencies within AI models. “To identify threats before attackers do, we must first understand what is inside a system,” said Bang Hyuk-joon, chief executive officer of Coontec. “We will continue enhancing AEZIZ so that public-sector and financial customers can identify risks in software components and AI models before deployment and respond as quickly as possible.”

title: Last Orders in the Alps: Riding a BMW R 1300 GS through the Dolomites - Autocar India
content: Somewhere on the approach to Passo Falzarego, I kept the throttle open well beyond the sensible braking point, then feathered the brakes far too late and tipped the fully loaded 250kg BMW R 1300 GS into a corner. The horizon tilted at what felt like 49 degrees. The motorcycle took it all in its stride. The suspension swallowed the bend; when I rolled back onto the throttle, the Akrapovič exhaust cleared its throat, the traction control moderated the conversation between the drive shaft and the rear wheel, and the front wheel lifted in a little wheelie of triumph. I carried on to the next hairpin with a smile plastered across my face, as it had been so many times that week. Around me, the Dolomites were having the best week of their year, in the middle of October. The larches had turned gold and rust, the pale rock towers stood bathed in sunshine, and the tarmac was dry and, for long stretches, entirely ours. Every so often another rider came the other way, two fingers held out in the wordless handshake motorcyclists everywhere seem to have agreed on. And there, around the next hairpin, a thought arrived, uninvited and slightly absurd: all of this had begun with an innocent phone call from Abhijit, my brother-in-law. Abhijit was twiddling thumbs between jobs, with time on his hands and a recently purchased Ducati Multistrada V4S standing in his parking bay. He called me for advice on where to take it for a road trip. The conversation wandered from Goa to Rajasthan, and to Kerala, but none of that caught his fancy. Then he said, “What about riding to Ladakh?” I told him that riding in Ladakh is wonderful, but getting there from Mumbai is tiresome. “It’s not like Europe,” I said rather offhandedly, “where riding from Munich to the Alps is almost as enjoyable as riding in them.” That was the tipping point. The Alps stuck to the conversation like a rash, and the mere mention of them infused my voice with a whole new level of excitement and elation. By the end of the call, what had started as Abhijit’s search for a week-long ride had turned into a plot in which I had committed to planning a 12-day loop out of Munich through Germany, Switzerland, Italy and Austria, with me becoming a party to the plan. Those eight minutes on the phone ultimately ended up costing me Rs 2.5 lakh – money very well spent! Then I started looking for a motorcycle. My first instinct was to find something in the 600cc to 800cc category. But my former Autocar India colleague, Ouseph Chacko, now a BMW-certified GS instructor, and Rishaad Mody, this magazine’s motorcycle editor, were unanimous in their advice: “Take the BMW R 1300 GS. It’s a sweet, sweet motorcycle.” That was all the convincing I needed. I asked BMW for one, and they said yes. Abhijit also chose the GS and rented one for the trip. To plan our ride, I hopped, skipped and jumped between Google Maps, Auntie Claude and Booking.com, checking distances, looking for route advice and good food, and finding mostly affordable two-bedroom apartments with free cancellation as close to the day of stay as possible. Now, on a bend near Passo Falzarego, with the larches blazing, the great limestone walls of the Dolomites bathed in warm, slanting sunlight, and the road empty beneath a motorcycle that was mine for twelve days, I smiled wistfully at the phone call that had started it all. Nine days earlier, I had stepped off an Etihad flight in Munich after an intentional 24-hour break in Abu Dhabi, so I met the GS without a trace of jet lag. The comfortable cabin, attentive service and warm hospitality onboard meant I swung a leg over the saddle well rested and energetic. We left Munich and rode south, deeper into Bavaria, the Alps growing larger in my visor until Wallgau, a village of timbered balconies and painted house fronts, appeared at their foot. For dinner that evening at the Gasthof Zur Post, I did what any traveller in Bavaria is duty-bound to do and ordered the pork knuckle. It arrived beneath a cap of crackling the size of a small cushion and left as bare bones. The next day, Austria’s Fernpass and Reschenpass unspooled in long, flowing curves, easy miles in which to settle into the GS before the real work began. Then we dropped into the Italian part of Tyrol and spent two nights in Laces, in the Vinschgau Valley, among apple orchards so laden that the branches were propped up on crutches. This also meant delicious apple strudel at most places we ate at. Carrying on, we crossed into Switzerland, over the Ofenpass and through the Swiss National Park, on a road lined with pine forest and almost no traffic, before dropping down to Poschiavo, with the Bernina Pass on its doorstep. I had set the mode button to toggle between Dynamic for the long, easy stretches, Dynamic Pro for the passes, and Rain for wet-weather days. By then, my thumb knew which one to reach for before my head did. Crossing back into Italy, we spent a night near Bormio, and the next morning we came face to face with the mighty Passo Stelvio sitting at 2,757 metres (9,045 feet). We rode the famed 48 hairpins of the north face. At the Tibet Hütte, the café at the summit, I ate apple strudel with fresh cream and watched cyclists grind up the last bends under their own power, grunting at the effort. I prayed to the Almighty to cure them of this affliction that makes them torture themselves and took another bite of my delicious dessert. At the bottom of the Stelvio, we turned east through the Vinschgau, past Merano and Bolzano, and powered on to Villandro and the Dolomites. Rumpelehof stands in the hamlet of Stofls, on the outskirts of Villandro. It is a working farm with self-catering apartments, where Alexandra and Raimund Gasser raise cattle and sheep. Mornings began with bleats and bull bellows rather than an alarm. Our two-bedroom apartment looked straight across at the Dolomites, a spectacular view, especially at sunrise. There were apple trees on the farm, and Raimund told me I could eat the apples without washing them because no pesticide had been sprayed on them. The only thing to watch for was worms. They were delicious, the apples, not the worms. For dinner on both evenings, we rode down to Gasthof Pizzeria Rustica in Villandro, a sprawling, warmly lit place that unfolds room after room, each one fuller and louder than the last. We came across two lads from Punjab working in its kitchen and had a hearty conversation with them. It was hunting season, so game crowded the menu. One night I ate a pizza with local salami and fiery peppers, the heat sneaking up like a rumour. The next, I had tagliatelle with a deer ragù – rich, slow-cooked, laced with pepper and finished with Parmigiano Reggiano – that I would happily have crossed a mountain pass for. Fortunately, I only had to ride down a hill. On our first day there, we rode a loop from the farm through Ponte Gardena, Ortisei and Selva, then up Passo Sella to Canazei, over the Pordoi and back the same way. The Alps had been wonderful, but it was the Dolomites that took my heart, perhaps because we arrived just as the autumn colours peaked. Near Canazei, through my helmet, I heard a familiar thump. My heart told me what it was before I turned my head. Sure enough, a Royal Enfield was chugging up towards Passo Pordoi. I excitedly flagged it down. The rider, from Lake Garda, said he loved everything about India and Royal Enfield. Around us were Multistradas, GSs and Africa Twins, while this humble Bullet chugged up the slope, holding its own, its rider in no hurry at all. The two engines could hardly have been more different. His Bullet, a single cylinder that thumps. Mine, a boxer, with two cylinders poking out either side like elbows at a crowded table, a layout BMW has been refining since 1923. Blip the throttle at a standstill and the GS rocks sideways, like a large dog shifting its weight. Both are unmistakable, and both certainly have character. It was the kind of day that leaves you a little melancholic and nostalgic, quietly happy at the way things have turned out. So, the next morning, when I leaned the GS into the hairpin on the road to Falzarego that opened this story, my mind went back to Abhijit’s phone call and how a casual conversation about Ladakh had brought me here. Mornings at that altitude start with a nip in the air, which is where the GS earns some of its keep. Thumb the heated grips and seat into life, and within two minutes you are sitting on a warm bench with warm hands, wondering why anyone ever thought bravery had anything to do with riding Alpine passes in mid-October. The other quiet hero was the BMW Motorrad ConnectedRide Navigator, the GPS unit above the dash, which I came to treat as a third member of the expedition. It is controlled by the rotary dial just ahead of the left grip, so I never had to take a glove off or a hand off the bars. I had loaded the daily routes I’d planned at home. Twelve GPX files, one for each day, went in through the BMW Motorrad Connected app, and every morning, the unit simply knew where we were going. Better still, it let me tell the motorcycle what kind of road I wanted: very twisty, moderately twisty or sensibly straight. I could ask it to avoid motorways and toll roads altogether. Where an ordinary satnav would have hustled us down the fastest road, this one, with a little encouragement from my thumb, kept finding the road worth riding. Over twelve days, it took us on a string of roads I would never have found on my own. That was how we found the road to Passo Falzarego and a procession of bends I’d happily call unreasonable, in the best way. Auntie Claude had warned me of the possibility of closed passes and snow. The passes, evidently, had not got her memo. Falzarego led to Passo Giau, which, as many riders will agree, is the most beautiful pass in the Dolomites. The road climbs through hairpin after hairpin into a wide, bare bowl ringed by rock, and the GS went up it as if it had been waiting all week for the invitation. Part of the secret is the boxer’s low, wide cylinders, which pull the centre of gravity down, so a motorcycle this heavy turns in like something much lighter. I braked late, leaned into corners at angles that would make Newton neurotic and got back on the throttle early, delighted by the feel of the front wheel lifting. We stopped at the top for coffee and cake, the two BMWs parked in the sun and preening. From there, we descended through Val di Zoldo, stopping at Rifugio San Sebastiano for a hearty salami and cheese sandwich and indulgent hot chocolate on Passo Duran, then continued to Venas di Cadore. We were meant to stay the night in the town of San Vito di Cadore, but our booking was cancelled because my credit card payment hadn’t gone through. It turned out to be the best thing my card did all year. A last-minute scramble found us a room at Dolomiti Lodge Villa Gaia, in a village ten kilometres away, and it became the best stay of the trip. We walked in expecting a bed and a plate of pasta. We walked out feeling like regulars at a village wedding. Dinner that evening at the lodge’s restaurant felt like one long communal table. Everyone talked to everyone, even to us, though we knew no Italian, rounds of drinks were bought for us, and people drifted over to say hello. Most of the diners were locals who knew the staff, but nobody treated us as outsiders. The staff came from Albania, Italy, Pakistan and Bangladesh, and they worked the room like a well-rehearsed dance. Music played, feet skipped between tables, and now and then a waitress broke into a small pirouette on her way to the kitchen. It was joyful, noisy and entirely unpretentious. The food kept pace. I opted for the wild pigeon, a bird I was trying for the first time. Where I come from, pigeons are treated as a civic nuisance, so there was a certain poetic justice in the exercise. It was really very good. Villa Gaia was the southernmost point and the happiest evening of our trip, and without anyone saying so, it became the hinge. From there, every road pointed north and back towards Munich. We still rode some glorious ones: from Cortina into East Tyrol, a night at Bergmanns Ferienapartment in Debant, a day on the Grossglockner High Alpine Road in Austria, then Kitzbühel and St. Johann in Tirol. The colours stayed blazing, the roads stayed dry, and the GS kept doling out delight. But the mood of the trip had undergone a subtle change. The days that had begun with a hunger to reach the next pass now began with the gentle awareness that this was the home run, and that real life, with its emails and credit card bills, was waiting somewhere beyond the Bavarian border. It is an odd feeling, fully enjoying something and mourning it at the same time. And then we rolled back into Munich, and I hauled the BMW R 1300 GS onto the main stand for the final time. Twelve days earlier, I had been apprehensive about handling this big motorcycle. Now I unloaded my luggage with the sort of reluctance people usually reserve for goodbyes at airports. I gave the tank one last pat, fondly, and walked away. The Key Monastery blends into Spiti’s spectacular landscape. title: GS Law mobilizes 2nd regional leg of West PH Sea Maritime Security Forum in Tarlac - University of Santo Tomas
content: The UST Graduate School of Law, in collaboration with the Tarlac State University School of Law, concluded the 2nd Regional leg of the West Philippine Sea Arbitral Ruling Forum on November 6, 2026, at the Old SP Session Hall, Capitol Building in Tarlac. The title of the second forum was “Upholding Sovereignty Through Law: Diplomacy, United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), and the Rationale of the 2016 Arbitral Award.” Former Supreme Court Associate Justice Hon. Francis H. Jardeleza and Atty. Jewel Dela Cruz shared their expertise as speakers, with Atty. Carisa Balilia providing thoughtful insights as a reactor. The lecture gave enriching perspectives on the legal, diplomatic, and historical foundations of the Philippines’ maritime rights in the contested sea. The initiative aimed to mobilize Filipino voices and entrusted the potential second case against China to the youth. Jardeleza served as the Solicitor General (2012–2014) and led the Philippine legal team in the landmark UNCLOS maritime arbitration against China. The first Regional Leg of the forum, titled “Batangas Securing the Maritime Frontier: Strategic Defense,” was held last Oct. 23, 2026, in collaboration with the University of Batangas College of Law. Anchored on the overall theme “Upholding Sovereignty Through Law: Diplomacy, UNCLOS, and the Rationale of the 2016 Arbitral Award,” the program brought together an engaged audience of law students, fisherfolk, TSU officials, the Armed Forces of the Philippines, legal practitioners, and advocates for an insightful and meaningful discussion. The third and last leg, titled “People at the Frontline: Building Resilient Coastal Communities amid West Philippine Sea Tensions”, will be staged at the Palawan State University on January 29, 2027. With support from the Public Diplomacy Section of the U.S. Embassy in Manila, the caravan kicked off at the UST on Sept. 25. 2026. title: LG Uplus, GS Neotek Team Up on End-to-End Security - Seoul Economic Daily
content:
U+SASE to Link With Security Lens
Partnership Aims to Ease Security Operations for Corporate Clients LG Uplus (032640.KS) is strengthening its end-to-end security portfolio covering customer devices, networks, cloud and servers through a partnership with GS Neotek. LG Uplus said on the 10th that it had signed a memorandum of understanding with GS Neotek to combine the two companies' network and cloud security capabilities. LG Uplus will contribute security monitoring capabilities built through its nationwide telecom network and data center operations, while GS Neotek will provide expertise in building and operating corporate cloud systems and managing server and data security. The two companies will first work to link U+SASE, LG Uplus's cloud-based integrated network and security platform, with Security Lens, GS Neotek's cloud security service. Under the arrangement, U+SASE protects user devices, networks and web access, while Security Lens inspects and manages the security status of servers and data within the cloud. The companies expect the tie-up to reduce the burden on corporate clients of building separate, fragmented security services and to make it easier for them to operate their security environments. The two plan to expand cooperation to Alpha Key, a cloud-based integrated account management solution; U+Safe AI, a data loss prevention solution designed for artificial intelligence; and managed detection and response (MDR) security monitoring. They also agreed to develop specific business cooperation models, including the resale of security products and joint sales activities. "Together with GS Neotek, we will provide easy and convenient end-to-end security services that reduce customers' security operating burden and allow them to focus more on their core business," said Kwon Yong-hyun, executive vice president and head of LG Uplus's enterprise division. Nam Ki-jung, chief executive of GS Neotek, said, "By combining GS Neotek's expertise in building and operating cloud systems with LG Uplus's network security capabilities, we will provide customers with a more complete end-to-end security environment." title: LG Uplus and GS Neotek team up to offer end-to-end cloud security - Chosunbiz
content: Partnership links U+SASE with GS Neotek's Security Lens so enterprises can manage device-to-cloud protections in one place, easing security operations LG Uplus is partnering with cloud specialist GS Neotek to target the integrated security market covering everything from user devices to networks, cloud, and servers. The strategy aims to meet increasingly complex security needs as more companies move to the cloud and use artificial intelligence (AI). LG Uplus said on the 9th that it signed a strategic memorandum of understanding (MOU) with GS Neotek for cooperation in the security business at LG Uplus's Yongsan office in Yongsan District, Seoul. The signing was attended by Kwon Yong-hyun, head of the Enterprise Business Division (executive vice president) at LG Uplus, and Nam Ki-jung, CEO of GS Neotek. The two companies plan to combine their technologies and business capabilities to build an end-to-end (E2E) security framework that protects every layer—from user devices that access corporate systems to networks, cloud, and servers. LG Uplus has nationwide networks, data center operations experience, and security monitoring capabilities. GS Neotek has built cloud security expertise by supporting many companies in building and operating their clouds. The setup expands LG Uplus's strengths in telecom and network security into security for servers and data inside the cloud. To start, the companies will link GS Neotek's Cloud-Native Application Protection Platform (CNAPP+) service, Security Lens, to LG Uplus's cloud-based network and security integration platform, U+SASE. U+SASE protects user devices, networks, and web access, while Security Lens checks and manages the security of servers and data inside the cloud. By combining them, the plan is to let enterprise customers run an integrated security environment without adopting multiple point solutions separately. They will also expand the scope of cooperation. The joint portfolio will include the cloud-based unified identity and access management solution AlphaKey, the AI-specific data loss prevention (DLP) solution U+Safe AI, and managed detection and response (MDR) security monitoring. They will develop concrete business models such as security product resale and joint sales. LG Uplus plans to use this partnership to strengthen its Telco-Native security strategy that combines networks, data centers, cloud, and security capabilities. The company aims to reduce enterprise customers' security operations burden by providing integrated services from planning to deployment and operations. "As corporate work environments grow more complex, customers face a heavier burden of building and operating multiple security services," said Kwon Yong-hyun, head of the Enterprise Business Division at LG Uplus. "Together with GS Neotek, we will offer easy, convenient E2E security services that reduce customers' security operations burden so they can focus on their core business." "As cloud use expands, a security framework that protects seamlessly from the user access stage to the inside of the cloud is becoming more important," said Nam Ki-jung, CEO of GS Neotek. title: The Buick GS Is the Muscle Car the Market Keeps Underpricing, and Hagerty’s Data Is Starting to Notice - Yahoo Autos
content: Buick's Gran Sport is the muscle car the market keeps forgetting to price. In its October Price Guide update, Hagerty reports 1968–72 Buick GS 400 and GS 455 values up 4% on average, the first meaningful gain after several quarters of declines. A single quarter is a modest signal. But it lands on a family of cars whose spread, from entry level to trophy, may be the widest in the segment. Our view: the GS is the clearest example of a muscle car that was priced for what it was not. It was never a Hemi or a Boss. It was a fast, heavy, torque-rich car from a company that did not shout, and the market is slowly learning to read that as a virtue. According to Hagerty's review, #2 (excellent) values across the 1968–72 GS 400 and GS 455 run from $27,700 for a 1972 GS 455 Sport Coupe to $129,000 for a 1970 GS 455 Stage I convertible. That is a spread of more than four and a half times inside one model family. Few cars in the hobby offer a collector a seat at the table for under $30,000 and a blue-chip option at more than $120,000 without changing badges. The 455 Stage 1 engine in a 1970 Buick Gran Sport. The air cleaner decal is visible, but the block code, casting numbers and carburetor number are what verify the engine. Photo: Mr.choppers via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0 The expensive end of the GS range is governed by the same forces as every other muscle car: engine, body style, documentation. A Stage 1 convertible is a different asset from a 1972 coupe, and the gap in Hagerty's numbers reflects it. That is why buyers should be careful about reading the 4% as a rising tide. It is an average over cars that behave very differently. We have seen how much the details matter. As we explained in our report on a 1970 Buick GSX with no VIN of its own, a GSX cannot be proved from the VIN alone, and a genuine Stage 1 GS is a valuable car but not a GSX. The Stage 1 decal on an air cleaner is not proof of anything. The verification lies in the block code, casting numbers and carburetor number. Two readings are reasonable. The first is simple recovery: after several quarters of declines, buyers see a car with a strong build story priced well below its Detroit rivals. The second is the broader pattern we describe in our look at the October Price Guide, where cars with a verifiable story hold up while those depending on a single feature slip. The Buick sits between those camps. Its story is real but quiet. There is also the Buick halo. The turbocharged era that followed, led by the Grand National and GNX, gave the brand a performance credibility that older Gran Sports can borrow. Our list of the most expensive Buick GNXs ever sold shows how seriously collectors take that lineage once a car carries the right paperwork. Be skeptical of any claim of Stage 1 or GSX without documentation, and look to the numbers on the engine rather than the decal. Decide whether you are buying a driver or an asset; at the low end, a clean GS 455 is among the least expensive entries to real big-block torque in the segment, while the top of the range demands a paper trail. And do not treat a 4% quarter as a trend. Hagerty's own data shows a rebound after several quarters of losses. The market has yet to prove it is more than a pause. title: Goldman Sachs (GS) Stock Price Prediction: Momentum fades below short-term averages as Binance flow stays mixed - Blockchain News

Against that, the 1-hour taker buy/sell ratio of 0.8534 shows more aggressive selling than buying in the most recent flow. That matters because it means passive long ratios are not yet being confirmed by aggressive demand. If GS reclaims the $888 to $894 resistance band and holds above the 20-day average, the next test is the upper Bollinger area near $931.76. If it fails to regain that zone, the market is more likely to rotate back toward $871 and then $860, where the stronger support cluster sits. The cleanest invalidation of the current bounce is a loss of $860.00, because that would put the lower band and the recent range floor directly into play. title: 2027 Federal Pay Raise: Up to 6.7% for Some as OPM Expands Special Rates - www.myfederalretirement.com

Financial Planning Resources for Federal & Postal Employees Most civilian federal employees are headed for a 0% raise in January 2027, but the plan for law enforcement runs in the opposite direction. A Nov. 6 memo from the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) says employees already on the law enforcement special rate tables will receive 3.8%, while employees newly brought under those tables will receive about 6.7%, subject to pay caps and agency review. The memo implements a directive in the president’s Aug. 26 alternative pay plan, which freezes General Schedule (GS) base and locality pay at 2026 levels while ordering a 3.8% increase for covered law enforcement personnel through special pay authorities. The memo is CPM 2026-13, signed by Veronica E. Hinton, Associate Director for Workforce Policy and Innovation, and addressed to agency chief human capital officers. Its title says “Request for Information,” but agencies only need to respond in two cases: to opt out of the new coverage, or to send questions or comments. Both are due Nov. 25, 2026. OPM organizes the law enforcement special rates into three groups of tables. Where an employee lands determines the increase. In January 2026, everyone received a 1% base pay increase. Employees on Tables L001 through L140 also received a 2.77% special rate increase, which brought their total to 3.8% (1.038 ÷ 1.01 − 1). title: 'Great sadness' as much-loved Welsh shop to close after 21 years - Tivyside Advertiser
content:
A local business supplying the community with news, stationary, a post office and everything from toys to cleaning products will close after two decades. GS News has been trading in Newcastle Emlyn for 21 years. The shop sells a bit of everything from Cymru hoodies to loo roll as well as books, toys and Welsh and English greeting cards. It also hosts the town’s post office which moved there from a location across the road in May, 2015. GS News in Newcastle Emlyn will close next month after 21 years (Image: Google Street View) GS News announced “with great sadness” that it is closing next month. The closure comes following the sad and sudden passing of co-owner Barry Rogers last April. The last day of GS News trading will be Monday, December 21. “I had very much hoped to be able to continue to keep the shop and Post Office open for the sake of the town and the townspeople,” said owner Sue Rogers in a post on social media. “It had been my intention to do so for as long as I could. "However, lately I have found it increasingly difficult physically to cope with the additional work and attendant stress, and now realise I simply have to slow down for my own well-being.” She added: “Barry’s sudden passing came as such a shock, and has made me realise we can’t take our health and longevity for granted.” She thanked her staff and customers for all their support and apologised for any inconvenience caused by the closure. “I am truly sorry for the huge void the closing of the Post Office will leave in the town, and wish things could be different,” she said. “I would like to say a huge thank you to all our loyal customers who have been such a big part of our lives. “I also want to thank our wonderful staff who are so hard-working and always cheery. “They have been such an amazing help and support, particularly in these last months, and I could not have got by without them.” GS News is currently in contact with the Post Office to discuss alternative accommodation for the service. Goldman Sachs strategists warn that the U.S. stock market bull run is entering its final countdown, with 2027 facing the largest net equity supply shock since the bursting of the internet bubble in 2000, while cracks in the AI narrative and deteriorating liquidity are exacerbating market volatility risk. According to Woofun AI, Tony Pasquariello, global head of Goldman Sachs (GS.US)'s hedge fund business, has issued a clear warning: although the main uptrend in the U.S. stock market has not yet been broken, it has entered a countdown; he expects the S&P 500 index to complete one final rally before a turning point, after which 2027 will face the largest net equity supply shock since the bursting of the internet bubble in 2000. The three core variables that have driven the strong performance of U.S. stocks over the past four years—earnings growth, capital flows, and the AI narrative—have all deteriorated in their marginal direction simultaneously. In his latest weekly report, Pasquariello notes that although Goldman Sachs forecasts S&P EPS could still grow by about 18% in 2027, and the S&P 500's second-quarter earnings growth reached 33% with third-quarter growth expected to hit 35%—the fastest pace in 30 years outside post-recession recoveries—the market is highly sensitive to changes in these rates. He emphasizes that the tension between the second derivative and the first derivative is becoming increasingly complex, making it ever harder to envision earnings delivering the kind of upward convexity that has characterized recent years. The more critical variable is that Goldman Sachs's earnings forecast is highly sensitive to AI capital expenditures, and this week's developments have significantly increased the downside risk to that forecast; with earnings growth peaking, upward momentum is becoming unsustainable. Signals from the capital flow perspective are even more alarming. According to data compiled by Woofun AI, over the past 20 trading days, hedge funds have been selling global AI stocks at their fastest pace in more than five years, deviating from the mean by more than three standard deviations, with this week's sell-off entering a state of "full-blown panic." Buyers have also collectively pulled back: weaker corporate buybacks, shrinking demand from overseas investors, and mechanical follow‑sell behavior by quantitative strategies such as CTA all combine to create a "buyer's strike." Even more concerning is the supply pressure looming in 2027: Pasquariello explicitly notes that net new equity supply in U.S. markets is expected to reach its highest level since 2000. The confluence of large IPO pipelines—including SpaceX (SPCX.US) and Anthropic—and a shift in corporate cash flows (with priority now given to funding capital expenditures over share repurchases) will exert simultaneous downward pressure on both the supply and demand sides. title: Bengaluru to host first standalone Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians' conference on November 17-18 - The New Indian Express
content: BENGALURU: Bengaluru will host the first standalone Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians (CWP) India Region Conference in the country on November 17 and 18, bringing together around 150 women legislators from across India and representatives from 15-20 countries to deliberate on women's political leadership, cyber safety and capacity building. Announcing the event at a press conference at Vidhana Soudha on Monday, Karnataka Legislative Assembly Speaker G S Patil and Legislative Council Chairman Saleem Ahmed said the two-day event would provide a platform for women parliamentarians and legislators to discuss the challenges they face in public life and explore ways to strengthen their participation in legislative and decision-making processes. "This is a matter of pride for Karnataka. It is the first time that a standalone Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians conference of this nature is being organised in India, and Bengaluru has been chosen to host it," Patil said. The conference will be inaugurated by Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla and Chief Minister D K Shivakumar. Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman Harivansh, Deputy Chief Minister G Parameshwara and CWP India Region Chairperson D Purandeswari will also participate in the inaugural session. Around 150 delegates, including women MPs, MLAs, Members of Legislative Councils, Speakers and Deputy Speakers from various States and Union Territories, are expected to attend. Four women legislators from each State are expected to be represented. Representatives from 15-20 countries are also likely to participate. The conference will focus on two major themes — women's safety in the digital and cyberspace environment and strengthening the legislative skills and leadership capabilities of women representatives. The deliberations will cover cybercrimes against women, online harassment, digital abuse, misuse of artificial intelligence, deepfake technology, and protection of personal information and digital privacy. The discussions will also examine the challenges faced by women elected representatives in the digital environment. The second theme will focus on capacity building, including legislative procedures, lawmaking, policymaking, parliamentary debates, leadership development and the effective use of technology in legislative functioning. "Women's representation in legislative institutions is important, but it is equally necessary to strengthen their capabilities and ensure that they have a meaningful role in policymaking and governance. The conference will provide an opportunity to discuss the challenges faced by women legislators and share experiences," Saleem Ahmed said. He said the Karnataka Legislature had been asked to host the conference and the detailed agenda was being worked out in consultation with the Lok Sabha Secretariat and the CWP leadership. Purandeswari has constituted a committee of around 27-28 MPs, which has already held preliminary meetings in connection with the conference preparations, he said. The event will begin with the inaugural session at 11 am on November 17, at Banquet Hall in Vidhana Soudha, followed by deliberations after lunch. The valedictory session will be held at noon on November 18, with Governor Sudha Yadav participating. A curtain-raiser programme will be organised on November 14, with Chief Minister D K Shivakumar and CWP India Region Chairperson D Purandeswari unveiling the conference poster and outlining the preparations. Patil said Karnataka had accorded prominence to women's participation in public life and the conference would send a strong message on women's empowerment across the country. When asked about the absence of women in the State Cabinet, Patil said there were two  vacancies at present and women would be accommodated. As part of the conference-related programme, delegates will also be taken on a visit to Mysuru on November 19, including to Chamundi Hills. The conference is expected to provide a national and international platform to discuss ways of making legislative institutions more inclusive and strengthening women's leadership in democratic governance. title: [Exclusive] “Let’s capture the 2,800-trillion AI infrastructure market” ... POSCO, GS forge data center “alliance” - 매일경제
content:
POSCO and GS are joining forces to target the artificial intelligence data center (AIDC) market. They will combine POSCO’s steel materials and solutions with GS Group’s overseas sales and construction capabilities. Together, they aim to target the global data center market. According to industry sources on the 9th, POSCO and GS are pursuing business cooperation related to AIDCs. The partnership is expected to be formalized within this month. Although concerns about regulations on data center construction have grown since the recent U.S. midterm elections, the plan is to use the cooperation to strengthen each company’s business competitiveness and open up new markets to overcome sluggishness in existing demand industries. McKinsey & Company estimates that, of the investment needed to build AI data centers worldwide from 2025 to 2030, construction and development—including land, materials and site development—will amount to $800 billion (about 1,080 trillion won), while infrastructure—including power generation, transmission and cooling—will total $1.3 trillion (about 1,755 trillion won). This is a market that POSCO and GS, with their materials and energy supply capabilities, could seek to enter. Although the specific scope of the businesses and the projects involved have yet to be determined, areas of cooperation under consideration include supplying specialized steel products needed for data centers and power infrastructure, and identifying overseas projects, based on the companies’ existing businesses. POSCO established its Future Demand Development Office last July as part of its effort to become a specialized steelmaker covering AI- and power-related materials and solutions. The office serves as a control tower, moving beyond market responses organized by individual products to coordinate POSCO’s full range of products in response to demand across growth industries. Last month, POSCO separately formed an AIDC Demand Development Project Team and an ESS Specialized Solutions Project Team, and established a collaboration framework with affiliates including POSCO International, POSCO E&C and POSCO A&C. POSCO offers a range of materials and solutions, from structural steel for buildings to cold-rolled steel sheets for server racks, highly corrosion-resistant PosMAC, stainless steel for cooling pipes and electrical steel for transformers. It recently also developed an electromagnetic shielding steel sheet, “PosMAC Shield,” combining electrical steel and galvanized steel. Within GS Group, GS Global Corp., GS Engineering & Construction and GS Caltex are central to a range of capabilities related to data center construction, from connecting overseas supply chains to construction, cooling and power. GS Global Corp. opened a branch in Houston, U.S., last August and expanded its local sales network alongside its existing Los Angeles entity. It has built a network connecting local engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) firms with steel processors and distributors, and plans to step up support for winning orders and identifying new businesses starting next year. Drawing on experience with projects such as the Anyang Epoch Data Center, GS Engineering & Construction is building a business model that links investment, development, construction and operations. GS Caltex has strengthened its competitiveness in cooling technology by launching a dedicated cooling fluid to remove heat from data center servers. title: Upcoming BMW F 450 R & F 450 RR: Price Expectations - ZigWheels.com
content: BMW Motorrad recently launched the much-awaited Sport variant of the F 450 GS in India. It offers almost all the features of the top-spec Trophy variant without the ERC (Easy Ride Clutch) and at a slightly lower price of Rs 5.90 lakh (ex-showroom). However, that is still quite a premium for an adventure bike in the sub 500 cc category. The brand is also planning to bring the recently unveiled BMW F 450 R and F 450 RR to India by next year. Here’s what we expect them to cost. When BMW first unveiled the F 450 R and F 450 RR, we expected the streetfighter to be priced at around Rs 4.60 lakh, while the fully-faired RR was expected to cost Rs 4.75 lakh (both ex-showroom). However, things have changed since then, and both motorcycles are now expected to arrive with considerably higher price tags. The BMW F 450 R could be priced at around Rs 5 lakh, while the F 450 RR is expected to cost approximately Rs 5.20 lakh (both ex-showroom). The new expected pricing has been assumed as per the current pricing of the F 450 GS, as the F 450 R and F 450 RR are based on this adventure bike. This also means that their top-spec variants could easily touch the Rs 6 lakh mark, considering that the F 450 GS Trophy currently costs Rs 6.15 lakh (ex-showroom). For context, the Aprilia Tuono 457 is priced at Rs 3.99 lakh, while the fully-faired RS 457 costs Rs 4.26 lakh (both ex-showroom). This gives the Italian motorcycles a considerable price advantage even before the BMWs arrive. Another interesting fact is that the German brand will be manufacturing these new bikes in India. Considering this, we hope the brand keeps the pricing competitive rather than positioning these motorcycles at a significant premium over their Italian rivals. We also hope BMW introduces the non-ERC variants of both motorcycles right from the beginning, instead of bringing them to India several months after the initial launch. This would give buyers more affordable options and make the F 450 R and F 450 RR more accessible. Ultimately, BMW has some interesting motorcycles coming to India, but their pricing will play a crucial role in determining how well they compete against the Aprilia 457 twins.
